characters.summary: Brainiac is a hyper-intelligent coluan android/cyborg entity who travels the cosmos shrinking and bottling cities to preserve their knowledge before destroying their parent planets. He utilizes vast mental capabilities, telepathy, telekinesis, and advanced drone technology.

techniques: Army of humanoid robot probes (given red-sun ray guns in New Krypton)
Superman-level strength and speed (varies by body)

mechanisms: Force fields that withstand Superman's strongest blows
Downloading his consciousness into spare robotic bodies

weaknesses: Microscopic organisms and dirty environments can overwhelm him (Superman knocked him into a swamp)
Telepathic link to his ship: sudden separation briefly disables him
limitations: Telepathic/telekinetic powers depend on the body he occupies
Prolonged separation from his ship causes deterioration and power loss

sources.supports: Powers (shrink ray, probes, force fields, spare bodies, Byrne-era telepathy/telekinesis), Kandor bottling revealed in Action Comics #867, Action #866-870 fights with Superman, weaknesses (ship link, microorganisms).

feats.claim: Shrank and bottled the Kryptonian city of Kandor.
His force field withstood Superman's most powerful blows.

notableResults.note: Overpowered Superman at first, but Superman knocked him into a swamp where microscopic organisms overwhelmed him.

campaignTags.claim: Shrink ray, force-field belt and an army of robot probes.
John Byrne's post-Crisis version had telepathy and telekinesis, depending on the body he occupied.
Downloads his consciousness into spare robotic bodies when his body is destroyed.

unknowns: Corrected Action Comics #869 'loss': the cited source shows Superman winning in #868; in #869-870 Brainiac is teleported away by Brainiac 5.
Telepathy may not apply to every post-Crisis/New 52 body.

characters.summary: Nathaniel Adam is a military officer whose body is coated in the alien metal Dilustel, letting him generate vast nuclear energy as blasts, force fields and explosive 'bombs', absorb energy, and split and re-merge his own atoms. He is nearly immortal, very strong and durable, survives in space and resists magic.

techniques: Splitting and re-merging his own atoms

mechanisms: Dilustel skin (only the X-Ionizer can damage it)

weaknesses: Rupturing his skin causes an uncontrolled radiation leak with risk of atomic detonation
limitations: Absorbing too much energy throws him uncontrollably through time
Heavy power use can destabilize his molecular structure

sources.supports: Dilustel skin, nuclear energy powers, absorption and time displacement, magic resistance, weaknesses, and fights (Major Force, OMAC Prime, Superboy-Prime).

feats.claim: Let OMAC Prime absorb his energy, then reabsorbed it and overloaded his powers.
feats.citation: Justice League: Generation Lost (issue not stated in source)

notableResults.citation: Captain Atom (issue not stated in source)
notableResults.note: Killed Major Force after escaping Blüdhaven.

unknowns: Removed an unsupported 'Captain Atom #1 nuclear absorption' feat and a 'Superman/Batman #30' draw with Superman.
Removed 'electric': nuclear energy is not electricity (fire/ice/electric stay separate).
Removed 'natural-flight' for now: the cited page lists flight only for Allen Adam; add back with a source.

characters.summary: Leonard Snart is the methodical leader of the Rogues, utilizing a specialized absolute-zero cold gun to freeze targets instantly. He relies on tactical planning, absolute zero fields, and criminal cunning rather than physical super-powers.

techniques: Cold beam that freezes on contact
Cold field that stops targets in their tracks
Ice fields, stalagmites and ice grenades

weaknesses: Normal human physical durability when caught off guard
Dependence on his cold gun tech
limitations: Weapon can be broken or disarmed
Relies on regular maintenance and power cartridges for his cold gun

sources.supports: Cold gun functions, gear, New 52 powers and inertia field, Flash vol. 4 #6-7 win, Flash vol. 5 #15 loss.

feats.claim: An ice grenade froze all of Iron Heights.
feats.citation: Blackest Night tie-in (issue not stated in source)

notableResults.note: His New 52 inertia field slowed the Flash to human speed.
Flash beat Snart and the Rogues after the Mercury statue heist.

conditional.ability: Absolute zero projection and ice generation

campaignTags.claim: Wields a specialized cold gun capable of projecting absolute zero temperatures.
Uses custom-built cryogenic weaponry and gear.

unknowns: Removed an unsupported Flash vol. 2 #182 feat and a vague 'Flash #1' loss.
New 52 metahuman cold powers were later removed (Forever Evil).

characters.summary: Cassandra Cain is a master martial artist trained from birth as the ultimate human assassin. She reads body language to anticipate opponents' movements instantly, granting her near-precognitive combat awareness.

mechanisms: Reading body language to anticipate attacks

weaknesses: No superpowers: normal human vulnerability to bullets and heavy attacks
limitations: Early on she was mute and illiterate because of her upbringing

sources.supports: Martial arts mastery, body-language reading, Batgirl utility belt gear, speech/literacy, Lady Shiva duels (Batgirl #21, #25-26).

feats.claim: Took several bullets to save the life of a hired assassin.

notableResults.note: Shiva killed her within minutes and restarted her heart; Cassandra then beat Shiva but spared her.

campaignTags.claim: Batgirl utility belt: grappling hooks, batarangs, mini-explosives, tracking devices, smoke pellets.

unknowns: Removed an unsupported Batgirl #1 point-blank dodge and corrected the Shiva citation from #73 to #25-26.
Removed 'stealth': no documented stealth feat in the source.
Second Shiva duel (broke her neck) has no issue number in the source.

characters.summary: Selina Kyle is a master cat burglar and skilled street-level combatant. She specializes in stealth, whip-handling, infiltration, and acrobatic hand-to-hand fighting.

techniques: Martial arts (trained by the Armless Master)

weaknesses: Standard human vulnerability to firearms and blunt trauma
limitations: Purely human physical stats with no super-strength or durability

sources.supports: Expert burglar, gymnast, whip and claws; theft feats (Brave and the Bold #197, Batman #695); escapes from Batman (Batman #1-3); Film Freak.

feats.claim: Broke into her husband's private vault to retrieve her jewelry.
Stole the contents of a Falcone family safe.

notableResults.note: Defeated him after his murderous rampage.

campaignTags.claim: Broke into a private vault (Brave and the Bold #197) and stole the contents of a Falcone family safe (Batman #695).

unknowns: Removed an unsupported Catwoman vol. 3 #1 vault feat and a Batman #355 result.
Changed 'stealth' to 'infiltration': the source documents break-ins but no stealth feat as such.
Removed 'gadgets': a whip and glove claws are weapons, not gadgets.

characters.summary: Barbara Ann Minerva, bonded to the plant god Urzkartaga, has cheetah-like superhuman strength, agility, durability and potentially limitless speed, with claws sharp enough to cut Kryptonian skin. Her bite can turn others into cheetah-like beings.

techniques: Claws that cut through Kryptonian invulnerability

weaknesses: Curse-driven bloodlust and hunger for human flesh
limitations: Severe pain and physical disability in her human form

sources.supports: Powers (strength, agility, durability, limitless speed, claws cutting Kryptonian skin, transforming bite), curse drawbacks, Wonder Woman vol. 5 #18 origin.

feats.claim: Her claws can cut through Kryptonian invulnerability.

unknowns: Removed unsupported Wonder Woman vol. 2 #200 and #214 fights, and an invalid 'natural-flight: Not applicable' tag.
Needs a sourced comics fight result vs Wonder Woman.

characters.summary: Circe is an immortal and immensely powerful sorceress devoted to Hecate. She commands dark magic, reality-altering transmutation spells, mind control, and energy projection.
weaknesses: Her power depends on Hecate's soul; when it withdrew in War of the Gods she aged and crumbled to dust
limitations: Power tied to her patron Hecate

sources.supports: Bestiamorph transmutation, energy blasts, mind control, flight and teleporting herself and others, Hecate link; War of the Gods #1-4; Wonder Woman fights incl. vol. 2 #174-176 and Superman/Wonder Woman #14-17.

feats.claim: Killed Hermes, temporarily erased Diana from existence and conquered New Olympus.
Mind-controlled Superman into fighting Wonder Woman.

notableResults.note: Defeated in single combat at the Parthenon; Diana spared her.
Diana broke her control of Superman and they defeated Circe and Magog.

campaignTags.claim: Commands master-level sorcery granted by the goddess Hecate.
Transforms people into animals (bestiamorphs) and fires magical energy blasts.
Has mind-control powers; mind-controlled Superman (Superman/Wonder Woman #14-17).

unknowns: Removed an unsupported 'transformed a whole city' War of the Gods #1 feat.
Removed unsupported 'regeneration via divine patronage' and incantation requirements.

characters.summary: Basil Karlo began as a masked actor-killer, then injected himself with the blood of Preston Payne and Sondra Fuller to become the Ultimate Clayface: a mud body able to shapeshift and melt with a touch. In The New 52 he is a massive clay creature able to imitate any features but his own.
weaknesses: Overloading his powers (Batman and Looker sank him into the Earth's crust)
limitations: Cannot imitate his own original features (New 52)

sources.supports: Karlo's powers from Payne and Fuller's blood (shapeshift, melt with touch), New 52 mimicry, Detective Comics #40, #49, #604 defeats.

feats.claim: Gained the combined powers of Preston Payne and Sondra Fuller by injecting their blood.
feats.citation: Detective Comics (1989, leading to #604; issue not stated in source)

notableResults.note: They overloaded his abilities and he sank into the Earth's crust, surviving.

unknowns: Removed 'giant-sized' and 'size-change': the source calls the New 52 form 'massive' but documents no size (owner ruling: about 8 ft or more with a documented size).
Removed unsupported water, temperature and solvent weaknesses and a Detective Comics #478 result (that issue is Preston Payne's debut).

characters.summary: James Gordon is the GCPD commissioner, a special-forces veteran (a former Marine in The New 52), a skilled marksman, hand-to-hand combatant and expert detective who relies on police resources and determination rather than powers.
weaknesses: Standard human mortality and vulnerability to injury
limitations: Normal human strength, speed, and endurance

sources.supports: Skills and military background, No Man's Land, The Killing Joke kidnapping, and fights (Flass, Mr. Bloom).

feats.claim: Kept order in an isolated Gotham during No Man's Land and later shot the Joker in the knee after Sarah Essen's death.

notableResults.note: Kidnapped and caged by the Joker (who shot Barbara); rescued by Batman.

notableResults.citation: Batman: Legends of the Dark Knight Annual #2
notableResults.note: Beaten by Flass, who kidnapped James Jr.

unknowns: Removed 'pilot': driving police vehicles is not piloting, and the source mentions no piloting skill.
Removed unsupported police body armor.

characters.summary: Victor Stone is a cybernetic hero integrated with advanced alien Mother Box technology. He fights using sonic cannons, techno-pathic hacking, teleportation boom tubes, and high durability armor.

techniques: Sonic cannon / sound amplifier (shatters rock, deforms steel)

weaknesses: Internal systems can be fried by feedback (Apokolips)
limitations: Boom tubes depend on his Mother Box (New 52)

sources.supports: Sonic weapons, technopathy, boom tubes, flight, nano-regeneration, Mother Box; Apokolips (Batman and Robin #35-36), Grid (Justice League vol. 2 #29), Trigon.

feats.claim: Triggered a self-destruct in Apokoliptian computers, repaired himself after the feedback, and closed the boom tube, banishing Kalibak.

notableResults.note: Shut down Grid with the Metal Men.

campaignTags.claim: Fused with advanced cybernetic implants and alien technology.
Generates Boom Tubes for instant interplanetary and interdimensional teleportation.
Nano-regeneration lets him repair himself after severe damage.

unknowns: Corrected citations: Apokolips hacking is Batman and Robin #35-36 (not Justice League vol. 2 #6); Grid is Justice League vol. 2 #29 (not #30).
Removed 'robot-or-ai': he is a cyborg, not an AI.
Removed unsupported missile barrage, adaptive shielding and EMP weakness.
